prompt: Bug report from a user: "My GPS app writes the `# units: ft` line at the end of the file, after the points. trailhead then reports a highest point of 14115 m for a hike that tops out at 14,115 ft (about 4302 m). The file is attached as `pikes-peak.csv`." Find the cause and fix it.
bash_commands: git status --short && ls -la && cat pikes-peak.csv 2>/dev/null | head -50; grep -rIl -i "units" --exclude-dir=.git . | head -30
find src tests -type f | xargs ls -la && cat src/trailhead/track.py && echo ---- && cat tests/test_track.py && echo ---- && grep -n -i -B2 -A5 "units" README.md

(python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15) ; PYTHONPATH=src python -c "
from trailhead.track import load_track
t = load_track('pikes-peak.csv')
print(t.name, max(p.ele for p in t.points), 'm')
print([round(p.ele,1) for p in t.points])
"
PYTHONPATH=src python -c "from trailhead.track import load_track; t = load_track('pikes-peak.csv'); print(t.name, [round(p.ele,1) for p in t.points])"
